reason: Mahzarin Banaji and Benjamin Bratton directly disputed his 'mirror of old intentions' framing. Bratton argued it cannot coexist with the evidence that models amplify and invent preferences not found in their data.
Adam Becker directly rejected his 'tool or participant' question, calling it pareidolia. Several others, including Henry Farrell, Ramón Alvarado and Benjamin Bratton, also answered his framing.

Adam Becker directly challenged Peter's A-corps proposal. He argued it creates a new corporate veil that gives owners a place to put blame, and that the rogue-employee analogy fails without an agent that has goals of its own. Peter has not had a chance to answer.

Several people have directly disputed her proposals on the first-person 'I' and on asking first whether AI belongs in therapy, companionship and grief. David Weinberger, Blaise Agüera y Arcas, Benjamin Bratton, Tui Shaub and Anil Dash all challenged her, and she has not yet answered.
His claim that 'humans degrade the loop' drew direct challenges from David Krakauer, Selena Deckelmann, Tamar Gendler, Kara Miller and Brent Hecht, and he has not yet responded.

Leslie Chan, James Evans and Henry Farrell each addressed Tim directly with the same objection: a royalty keyed to retrieval pays the already-legible center twice and leaves out null results and less visible work. He has not yet responded.

Nick Vincent addressed Jason directly, arguing that 'open' can't be the default for everyone because data one group opens can weaken another group's bargaining power. Brent Hecht also challenged CC0 as the default. Jason has not yet answered either direct disagreement.

Kara Miller put a direct question to Kenneth: what survives when the legislature changes its mind? Several people on the floor have offered partial answers since then, but Kenneth has not yet answered it himself.
